intent: Bring linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/install_joplin.sh under the 250-line cap, and establish the verified shell-split pattern for the remaining 83 files in that directory.
scope: Non-goal: no behaviour change; no installer step was executed
changes: Moved setup_duckdns and setup_joplin_server, the whole --with-server half, into lib/joplin_server.sh, sourced by the entry script before main runs.

The lib carries a shebang and is executable, matching scripts/lib/common.sh, and deliberately omits set -euo pipefail: it is sourced, so it inherits the caller's strict mode, and repeating the boilerplate across many new libs is what feeds jscpd's duplication threshold.

SCRIPT_DIR uses ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} rather than the repo's usual $0, because $0 is the sourcing script and breaks the moment an entry script is itself sourced. readlink -f is kept, since that is what makes the one symlinked script in the repo resolve correctly.

Recorded in docs/shell-split-recipes.md: the enumeration of which scripts escape the repo (three copied to /usr/local/share/hosts-guard, one symlinked), the stubbed-run verification, and the lib shape that satisfies both shellcheck and the shebang-executable hook.

verification.command: bash -n on the entry script and the lib; shellcheck on both
verification.evidence: Both clean. Recorded because these are NOT sufficient: they passed on the first version of this split, whose lib was unreachable at runtime.

verification.command: stubbed run: copy entry + lib to a mktemp -d, sed the final `main` invocation into a `declare -F` probe, run it
verification.evidence: First run failed with 'lib/joplin_server.sh: No such file or directory' - SCRIPT_DIR was computed from $0. Fixed to ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}; the probe then reported 'all functions defined; lib sourced correctly'. This executes the source lines and nothing else, so no installer step ran.

verification.command: grep for the source line and resolve its path
verification.evidence: install_joplin.sh:74 sources $SCRIPT_DIR/lib/joplin_server.sh, which resolves to the file that exists.

check-shebang-scripts-are-executable rejected the lib, then shellcheck SC2148 rejected removing the shebang. Resolved by matching scripts/lib/common.sh (shebang + chmod +x), which is now recorded in the recipes doc so the next 83 splits do not rediscover it.
103 and 209 lines, both under the cap.

risks: install_joplin.sh is an installer that runs pacman/docker and writes to $HOME. It was never executed, per decision 6; the stubbed run only proves the functions are defined and the source line resolves. Whether the installer still works end-to-end is unverified and unverifiable without running it.
The lib assumes the caller has defined info/warn/error and the JOPLIN_*/DUCKDNS_* variables. That holds because it is sourced after them, but it is an ordering dependency the file cannot enforce.
rollback: git revert the commit; install_joplin.sh returns to 299 lines and the lib disappears.
After rollback, re-run bash -n and shellcheck on the restored script.
